A LITTLE CONTEXT

How to convert REM to PX

Multiply the rem value by the computed font size of the root element, usually <html>. With a 16px root, 1.5rem × 16 = 24px. With a 20px root, the same 1.5rem is 30px. Enter the root size used by your own page above.

px = rem × root font size

References: MDN: CSS length units

Good to know

How many pixels is 1rem?

1rem equals the computed root font size. It is 16px when the root is 16px, 20px when the root is 20px, and 10px when the root is 10px. Browser defaults, page styles and user settings can change it.

Can I convert several REM values at once?

Yes. Enter up to 1,000 numbers without unit suffixes, separated by spaces, commas, semicolons or new lines. Copy the results in the same order, or download a CSV containing each input, root size and output.

Does this measure physical screen pixels?

No. The result is a CSS pixel length. Device pixel ratio, browser zoom and display density affect how CSS pixels map to physical screen pixels.

Will the tool rewrite my stylesheet?

No. It converts numeric values only. It does not parse CSS, change your site or replace rem units in stylesheets. Results use standard JavaScript numbers and are rounded to the selected 0–8 decimal places.

PRACTICAL REFERENCE

REM to PX examples

These examples use a 16px root. The live conversion and table above recalculate when you change the root size.

1rem and 1.5rem to pixels

1 × 16 = 16px. For 1.5rem, multiply 1.5 × 16 = 24px. If the root becomes 20px, 1.5rem becomes 30px.

1.25rem to pixels

1.25 × 16 = 20px. At a 10px root the result is 12.5px; at a 20px root it is 25px. The rem value stays the same while its pixel length changes.

0.75rem to pixels

0.75 × 16 = 12px. At a 20px root this is 15px. A fractional rem value can produce a fractional CSS pixel value; choose enough decimal places for your task.

0.875rem to pixels

0.875 × 16 = 14px. At a 20px root this is 17.5px. These examples explain the arithmetic; they are not recommendations for readable font sizes.

PRACTICAL REFERENCE

Find the root font size on your page

Open the browser developer tools on the page you are building. Inspect the computed font-size of its <html> element, or run this read-only expression in that page’s console.

Read the computed root size

getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).fontSize
// Example result: "16px"

Use that pixel value in the root-size field. Do not assume a site uses 16px: a percentage, media query or user preference can change the computed root size. Converting to pixels does not by itself make a layout accessible. For the reverse calculation, open PX to REM.
